## Example 3.4 · Which households count? {#l2-example-3-4-events }

| Pets, $x$ | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Frequency, $f$ | 15 | 20 | 10 | 4 | 1 |

c) What proportion of households own exactly 2 pets?
d) What proportion of households own 2 or fewer pets?
e) If a household is chosen at random, use the table to estimate the probability that they own at most 3 pets, $P(X\leq3)$.
<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 39 · Example 3.4 · Complete the working in your booklet.</p>

::: notes
(c) 10/50 = .20. (d) (15+20+10)/50 = .90. (e) 49/50 = .98. Identify the event before selecting the table column. Use relative frequency as the empirical estimate; no claim about every household outside the surveyed group is warranted.
:::
